issue.title: Amounts without a leading zero (.75) are rejected
issue.body:
Our payroll provider's export writes amounts under one euro without the zero in
front: `-.75` for a bank fee, `.50` for an adjustment. Every such file fails
with 'The amount is not a number' at the first row like that (row 14 in
October's file). Changing them to `-0.75` and `0.50` by hand makes the file
import. Larger amounts in the same file, like `-1,204.10`, are read correctly.

input.title: Accept amounts with no leading digit (.75, -.75) in parseAmount
input.body:
File: src/util/money.ts

The validation regex in parseAmount, /^\d+(\.\d+)?$/, requires at least one digit before the decimal point, so amounts like ".75" or "-.75" return null and the ingest step reports errors.badAmount. Change the check so a fraction without a leading integer part is also accepted, for example /^(\d+(\.\d+)?|\.\d+)$/. The sign handling already runs before this check, so "-.75" becomes -75 minor units as expected.
